title: The light show, one tap away
changes: “Light show” is the first chip under Hub's greeting, and on House it sits after the scenes. It opens your playlists, and one tap starts the show. Its card then leads Ask, with the music, the timing and End show.

title: Lamplight: Hub, redrawn
changes: Hub has a new look: a warm night and warm paper by day, Hub speaking in a serif voice of its own, and lit rooms that glow like windows seen from the street, as bright as their lamps.
Behind Hub's greeting, a slow band of warm light drifts like lamplight through a window at night. It is warmer the more rooms are lit, and the kitchen wall has it along the bottom.
One bar at the bottom instead of four: Ask, House and Dashboards, with the record that is playing and its pause beside them. Suggested messages sit at the end of what Hub says first.
Every page opened from Ask has its way back at the top left, and the phone's back gesture works. Pull a sheet down to close it.
After "dim the kitchen", the room's brightness is right under the answer to set it just so.

title: Ask's message field stays in sight
changes: On a phone, Ask’s message field stays above the music bar after the wall has been opened; it used to slip under it.

title: Light shows from Ask
changes: Ask starts a light show when you ask for one with a playlist, album, artist or song. When your words could mean several, it shows them on a card and starts the one you tap.
Ask ends the show when you ask. Playing music never starts one.

title: A light show card in Ask
changes: While a light show is running, its card sits at the top of Ask: what it plays, pause and next, its volume, the lights a step earlier or later against the music, and End show.
On a laptop, Ask fits beside the house again, so its Send button is never cut off.

title: Nothing hidden counted
changes: The look over Hub after each update no longer measures what a closed fold hides, and Trip’s links in an opened fold are easy to tap.

title: Easier to tap on a phone
changes: Every button, tab and link Hub shows on a phone is at least 44 points tall, a finger’s width, on the older pages too: Ask’s folded messages, a recipe’s name, the older Today, Kitchen, Mail, Trip, Bike + bus and class guide pages.

title: Fewer false alarms after an update
changes: The look over Hub after each update no longer flags things scrolled out of view inside a box, or the wall’s slow drift that keeps the kitchen iPad from burning in.

title: Shorter pages, plainer words
changes: Kitchen shows each thing that needs a pick with its likeliest product and “2 more choices”, and its button says “Pick · $4.79”.
Versions lists the newest six, with the rest one tap away.
Mail shows a sender with no name by their site, not their address.
The Network dashboard says “Traffic now” and how “Right now” was checked in plain words.
In the day look, highlighted titles are a readable amber, and the older Kitchen page’s message field sits above the music bar.

title: Times from the house on your clock
changes: When Ask says when a scene last ran or an automation last fired, it gives the time on the household’s clock, not in UTC.

title: A look over Hub after each update
changes: After each update the Mac mini walks through every screen of Hub at phone and laptop size, only looking, and keeps a short note of anything hard to tap, hidden under a bar or failing. It never holds or undoes an update.

title: House and System, plainer
changes: On a phone each room shows its way in, and a tap on it opens the room without switching its lights.
A light bridge’s many presets fold into one chip that opens them, and on a wide screen the rooms come first.
System says “All good at home.” or how many things need a look, and its sections have plain names.
A lock or door that stops answering shows “Not answering”, and the wall opened on a phone has a way back.

title: Ask, easier to read and to get around
changes: Ask draws a model’s lists and bold words instead of showing their marks.
When Kitchen is asked two things at once, each answer lands under its own question.
Today and Kitchen are one tap from Ask’s start, the greeting has Open Today, and Return on a page’s first letters opens it.
A question about bills brings only bills, and with no bank connected Ask looks in mail for them first.

title: Quiet your loudest senders, in Mail settings
changes: Mail settings lets you quiet your loudest senders one at a time: how many are in the inbox and how many unread, the last few subjects, and whether a filter already skips the inbox. Nothing changes in Gmail until the plan is applied.
The older Mail overview and labels pages open the Mail dashboard.

title: Touch a chart to read it
changes: Touch either pregnancy chart to read it: the chance at any week, or a day’s chance of labour and the share by then.

title: The chance of a live birth, and when babies come
changes: The pregnancy dashboard shows the average chance of a live birth from here and how it rises week by week, when babies are usually born by date, and a day-by-day curve around the due date, each with its sources.

title: The pregnancy dashboard, clearer
changes: The pregnancy dashboard calls its due date an estimate until the dating ultrasound, and its Settings button changes it in one tap.

title: Ask searches the family archive
changes: Ask can search the family’s photos, documents, mail, calendar history and ChatGPT history, and says where each answer came from.
It shows the month’s best photos and photos from this day in earlier years on a card Hub draws itself; nothing about a photo reaches the model.
The archive needs its helper installed on the Mac, with Full Disk Access and Photos access; until then Ask says it isn’t set up.

title: More room for asking
changes: Ask’s monthly budget is $100 now, up from $10.

title: Your career desk, in Ask
changes: Career is a dashboard of your own: your thesis, your plan’s steps to tick, what you are writing, field notes and evidence. Nobody else sees it.

Ask can note something for your career in your own words, tick a step, look a topic up on the web for a field note with sources, or write a first draft. Hub never publishes, posts or applies for anything.

title: Hub’s builds leave less behind
changes: Checking a new version of Hub no longer leaves a few hundred megabytes behind on the Mac each time.

title: Dashboards on the phone
changes: On a phone, the bar at the bottom now has Dashboards beside Ask and House: one tap lists them, one more opens one.

title: Money, read and never moved
changes: Money is a dashboard: the month against the budget, spending by category, bills and paydays, goals, accounts and net worth.

Ask answers money questions (how the month is going, what was spent on something, can we afford it) and changes Hub’s own budgets, categories, goals and bills, each with Undo. Hub reads the banks and can never pay, transfer or trade.
Each of you connects your own banks on the Money dashboard, chooses which accounts are private, and whether Ask may use your money.

title: Ask tidies mail, after your tap
changes: Ask can archive an email, put it back in the inbox, label it or mark it read or unread: it shows a card naming each email, and nothing changes until you tap it. Undo is on the card for a day.

title: Ask plans trips by bike and bus
changes: Ask plans trips by bike or Lime and bus: ask how to get somewhere.

title: Older pages become dashboards
changes: Calendar and AI spend are dashboards now; the older Calendar and Insights pages open them.
Trip and School are dashboards too; the trip workspace and the class guide stay for changing them.
All tools and Settings now open System, which lists Status, Checks, Golden tests and Ask activity.

title: House health, steered from Ask
changes: House health, under System, shows what the house’s caretaker sees: what needs you, last night, each part of the house over seven days, ways to make the house sturdier, and batteries.

Ask answers “how’s the house?” from it and steers it: pause or resume it, run a drill, try a fix again, or mark a problem sorted. Restarting Home Assistant and leaving a problem alone still wait for your tap on the card.
What the caretaker hands you shows on Today and in the morning message, and the button at the top turns amber until it’s sorted.
When Hub is slow the first time Ask opens in the morning, the morning message now comes at a later opening instead of not at all that day.

title: Hub can update itself, and Undo puts the last update back
changes: Once switched on, Hub puts a new version live by itself when its checks pass, goes back by itself if a check fails after the switch, and tells you on your phone.
For a day after any update, Versions shows it with Undo, which puts the version from before back.
Today says when Hub updated itself, or why an update didn’t go live.

title: Hub checks itself more carefully after each update
changes: After each update, the test light is read back a few seconds after it is switched and again after it is put back, so a light that an automation switches straight back no longer passes, and one that isn’t back as it was is set back.
When the AI model is busy, Hub’s checks wait and ask again, and a model that stays busy no longer counts as a failure.
The check of Ask no longer trips over a room with two or more lamps on.

title: Dashboards in the side column
changes: On a laptop or iPad, the column on the left lists Dashboards and each dashboard under Ask and House, so one click opens Pregnancy, Network or Mail.

title: Ask answers what it’s asked, and Kitchen fills a Costco cart too
changes: Ask knows your music library: ask “what playlists do I have?” and it names them, or “play my Dinner playlist” and it plays that one. Making or deleting a playlist still waits for your tap on the Playlists page.
Ask can look up Hub’s own records: the trip, what the AI has cost, how full the inbox is, and the devices on the network.
Ask answers the question instead of a stock line, may give a short list when you ask for one, and when it can’t do something it says so and names the closest thing it can.
Hub keeps a record of every Ask turn: what it used and whether it answered, got stuck or failed, so bad answers show up instead of passing as fine. When the model is busy, Ask says so.
After each deploy, Hub now checks this Ask itself: it lists your playlists, plays one, turns a room’s lights off and answers a weather question.

Kitchen: each thing on the list goes to Fred Meyer or Costco. Costco things say so on the list, and one tap on a thing’s Store row moves it. Your carts has a link to each store’s cart, and what went into the Costco cart stays as it went in.

title: Dashboards: one page each for the pregnancy, the network and mail
changes: Dashboards: a page for each part of the household, found by typing a few letters in Ask or from System. Arrange puts the blocks in your order and hides the ones you don’t want, for you only.

Pregnancy: the week, the size, the trimester and days to go, what usually comes next (visits, screenings, vaccines) with dates, a getting-ready list you both tick, and month by month. The due date can be changed on the page.
Network: whether the internet is up, speed and ping now, the day’s drops and uptime, charts for the last day, and the busiest devices.
Mail: what needs you, the inbox over a month, what’s in it by kind, and what Hub’s cleanup has done.
Ask answers “how far along are we?” or “is the internet down?” with the dashboard under the answer, and Today ends with a line for each dashboard.

title: Ask reads your own mail, and the music sheet shows every music in the house
changes: Ask can search your own mail and read an email it found: ask “did the plumber write back?”, and the emails show under the answer, each with Open to go to it in Gmail. “Open the first one” reads it. Nothing changes your mail, and nobody else’s mail is searched.
When rooms play different things, the music sheet is now Music in the house: a card for each, with the song, the rooms it plays in, play or pause, next, and one volume for all its rooms.
Rooms on a card shows each room's own volume and takes a room out. Add a room brings in a quiet room, or moves one over from another song. Change music picks a playlist for just those rooms.
Quiet rooms sit at the bottom with Play here and Join. With two things playing, Join asks which one. With one thing playing, the sheet looks as before.
On a phone, Ask’s field stays above the music bar and the conversation scrolls smoothly under your finger, without the whole screen sliding.

title: Hub opens on Ask, with errands ready for a tap and the family brief on each phone and the kitchen wall
changes: Hub opens on Ask, and Ask is a chat: Hub speaks first, in a bubble, with the day in a sentence, what needs you with its circle and its button, and the house in a line with its scenes. Your messages are on the right in the lamp’s colour, Hub’s on the left, and the field says Message Hub.
The bar is two places, Ask and House. Today, Mail and Kitchen open from Ask: from its cards, from under an answer, or by typing a few letters of their name.
Asking what needs you, about mail, the calendar or school now ends in the same rows Today shows, to tick or open right there.
Suggested messages sit over the field until a conversation is going: what you often ask around now first. One tap sends it.

The field is ready the moment you tap it, stays above the keyboard, and grows to a few lines. Ask something while Hub is still on the last request and it waits its turn. Stop is there while Hub works.
The day’s conversation is still there when you open Hub again: earlier ones above, as small bubbles with their Undo.

Errands: each morning Hub reads the emails that need you, bills and renewals, invitations and the class guide’s to-dos, and gets each one ready for a tap: what to do, why, when it’s due, and the sentence it rests on.

A tap opens the place where it gets finished, already filled in: a reply in your mail app or Gmail, the event in Google Calendar, the sender’s own page to pay or renew, or a call. Things to buy go on the shopping list. Hub never sends, pays, books or orders anything itself.
Hub closes an errand by itself when it sees it done: your reply in sent mail, the event on your calendar, a receipt from the same site. Done, Tomorrow and Not this are one tap, each with Undo.
Today shows the errands ready for your tap and leads to the rest, and Ask can say what’s waiting.
Your errands are yours: each person sees only those from their own mail, plus the class guide’s, which are everyone’s at home. When one of you finishes a class to-do, it’s done for both.

Tell Ask “I paid the power bill”, “the photo form can wait till tomorrow”, “I don’t need the dental cleaning” or “put the pumpkin on the list”, and it does what the tap would, with Undo under the answer. It only acts on what your own words ask for.

Your mail and calendar are yours alone. On anyone else’s phone, Mail says their mail isn’t connected yet, and Ask, the older Gmail and Calendar pages and the inbox charts on Insights show them nothing of yours.
Chats on the older Ask page are each person’s own as well.
Preschool’s tools for your own mailbox, how far Hub files your mail on its own, and the overnight review are yours to use; the class guide and the shared school mailbox stay everyone’s.
Plan what’s missing on a recipe no longer sits on Planning. Kitchen’s answer shows right under the recipe: the cart plan with Add to cart and Not now, or what Kitchen said instead.
When Kitchen couldn’t answer, for example because its Claude plan was at its limit, the recipe says so and the button comes back to try again.

Today is the family brief: the weather drawn (now, when rain comes, what to wear, the next hours and days), every lock with its battery from Home Assistant and Apple Home, the alarm and the garage, the night’s word from the caretaker, school and the calendar. From five in the evening it turns to tomorrow.

Each of you sees your own Today: your mail, your calendar and the note are only yours, by the Tailscale login on your phone. The weather, the house, school, the trip and the household’s needs are everyone’s. Hub needs to know whose login is whose first (“people” in household.json).
A lock battery that is low or flat is one line in Needs you, the flattest first, with Add to list for the batteries it takes.

A short note at the top joins your brief’s parts, like rain that lands on a pickup. Ask’s model writes it from the weather, your calendar, school and the house, never mail or the shopping list, at most every half hour. "brief": {"note": false} in household.json switches it off.

The wall: open it on the kitchen iPad from System, The wall. A big clock, the weather, what needs the household and the house, kept fresh by itself, following the sun from day to dusk. It is the household’s only: calendars, school, mail and the note stay on your phones. At night it is a dim clock and tomorrow’s weather.
Ask knows the brief: ask about the weather, whether to take a jacket, or which lock needs batteries. The brief can also be read aloud from a Shortcut, from /app/api/brief.

What you ask Hub to remember is yours: your notes steer your own Ask and nobody else’s, and only you see, save or remove them. Notes saved before are the owner’s, and the overnight review follows the owner’s.

Ask is one conversation that keeps going. Scroll back through it by day, as far as three months. Hub keeps a short summary of what came before your last messages, so “what did we decide about that?” works days later.
Ask “what do you remember about our conversation?” to read that summary, or say “start fresh” to have Hub set it aside. Your messages stay on screen either way. Your conversation is yours alone.
There’s one place to talk to Hub now. Tell it things in Ask: “remember that …” for guidance, or “Hub should …” for something to build.

Each morning, the first time you open Ask, Hub says up to three things that need you, most pressing first: the house and bills before anything else. Answer by typing “done 2”, “not this” or “Thursday”, or tap its button. Today still has everything.

Ask “what are you watching?” to see what Hub looks after for you, and “stop watching …” or “watch … again” to switch one. Say “not this” twice to a small kind of thing and Hub leaves it out for a month; bills, deadlines and the house only go when you say so.

title: Ask sets up the house, and Kitchen is part of Ask
changes: Ask can change how Home Assistant is set up: move a light to another room, rename it, hide or disable it, add or remove a room, change a scene, make an automation or switch one off, set the thermostat, lock a door, make a dashboard, reload an integration that stopped answering.
It does these at once and says so in a sentence, with Undo under the answer, on Activity and on Changes, for a day.

Anything that removes or disables something, unlocking or opening a door, and settings for the whole house wait on a card for your tap. So does a scene or an automation that would unlock or open, however you ask for it. Typing yes does nothing.

Kitchen is part of Ask. Say “add sponges and two avocados to the list” and Hub picks the exact product you buy, from your past orders: your own line for it, or what you took most of the last five times. What it can’t be sure of waits for one pick, and Hub knows it next time.
A number counts single things, so “6 eggs” is one carton. Say a thing again with another number and it is changed. One fewer and one more are on each thing’s sheet.

The Kitchen screen is the list on its way into the cart: each thing, its product, where it stands, and what needs you. Recipes, the cart as its own page shows it and the order to place are drawn in Ask, under what you asked.
With “Fill the cart by itself” switched on, what you add in Ask, on the screen or on your Groceries reminders lands in the cart a minute later. Placing an order still takes your tap.
Two new checks on the Checks page prove all this on the real house without changing it: one reads what Ask’s setup tools read, the other asks Ask a few things with nothing sent.
The list needs the kitchen service’s own update. Until it has it, Kitchen still answers in words.

title: Everything that happened in the house
changes: Activity, under System, lists what happened in the house, newest first: lights, doors and locks, button presses, automations and music, from Home Assistant, Apple Home and Hub itself.
Each line says what did it when that's known: a person, an automation, or Hub with Undo. Apple Home never says who, so its lines don't either.
A device that both Home Assistant and Apple Home report shows once, and Hub keeps 90 days, longer than Home Assistant does.
Motion and everything else are a tap away, and the list can be narrowed to one source.

title: Music in another room, and every screen in the app
changes: Music in another room is one tap: the music sheet lists every room, and a quiet one has Play here, for music of its own that starts softly while the rest plays on, and Join.
A room's own panel offers the same, the bar at the bottom names rooms playing something else, and a room playing its own music has its own pause.
Deploy is in the app: Versions shows a new version with a Deploy button, says when Hub is updating, and reloads by itself when the new version runs.
Engine is a screen in the app: what you asked Hub for, notes and routines waiting for a tap, how far Hub may go, and what the models cost.
Mail's Rules and settings open in the app: the plan with Apply and Undo, how far Hub files each kind, the charge alert and the 30-day rules.
Everything Hub changed, in the house and in playlists, is a screen in the app, each change with Undo for a day.
The older pages wear the app's look and carry its tabs, so none of them looks or feels like the old Hub.

title: Buttons on the wall show in their room
changes: A wall or remote button shows in its room, with its last press, its battery and what each press does.
The developer page reads the projects folder, and shows its tmux and brief sections only when they are set.

title: The app becomes Hub's front door, with Mail and Kitchen
changes: Hub's usual address opens the new app. The older pages stay under System, and the old chat is at /ask.
A Versions page under System lists each release with what changed and links to the code.
Mail is a screen in the app: what needs you and who hasn't answered, then what Hub sorted, with filing and Undo.
Kitchen is a screen in the app: the conversation, recipes, cart plans, orders and the shopping list.
Ask can now read your mail, calendar and school details on Claude Sonnet to answer questions about your day.

title: The new app: Home, Music, Ask and Today
changes: The new app at /app: the house as a plan of rooms that light up, with music, scenes and Undo.
Ask inside the app, on Claude Sonnet, for requests about the house: say it and Hub does it.
Today inside the app: what needs you first, then the rest of the day.

title: Dev page fix
changes: The Dev page reads terminal window names that contain spaces.

title: Home Assistant inside Hub, and live checks
changes: Home Assistant and Music Assistant open inside Hub, behind Hub's sign-in.
Live checks: small tests of the real running system that a deploy must pass.
A Dev page with every project's live state.
Silent speakers fold under one line on the Music screen.

title: Ask plays the music it found
changes: When Ask finds music, it plays it instead of only naming it.

title: Ask lists the devices on the network
changes: Ask can list the devices on the home network, grouped by mesh unit.

title: Today's Home card leads to Music
changes: The Home card on Today leads to Music and Music Assistant.

title: A mini-player and a Music screen
changes: A mini-player on Hub's pages while music plays, and a Music screen under Home.

title: Rooms from Home Assistant, and a Now playing card
changes: Rooms come from Home Assistant's areas and labels, and light colours stay within bounds.
Ask shows a live Now playing card.
Home Assistant and Music Assistant are one tap away.

title: Hub gets a logo
changes: A logo, with every icon drawn from it. The empty Ask chat shows it.

title: A record of every Ask turn
changes: Each Ask turn is recorded, failed answers included, with an Ask activity page to look back at them.
Music plays only real items, checks that it started, and groups under the speaker already playing.

title: A new look
changes: A warm paper palette, raised cards, pill buttons and a segmented main menu.
A calmer Ask chat with a floating box to type in.
Icons on every tool, and charts on the new palette.

title: Cards in the chat, recipes and fix cards
changes: Ask shows cards in the chat, with an Improve this button.
Saved routines (recipes) of allowed steps, kept only when you tap to save.
"As well" plays music in sync across speakers.
A friction log, and morning cards offering fixes: Build, Not now or Never.
When a name is both a room and a device, Hub takes it to mean the room.

title: Ask plays music where asked
changes: Ask plays a specific pick, only on the speakers asked for, and softly when asked.

title: Playlists through Music Assistant
changes: Hub can make and change playlists in Music Assistant, with Undo and reminders.
Each background playlist edit is checked before the next one starts.

title: Hub can run the house
changes: Hub reads the house through Home Assistant and can change lights, plugs, scenes and speakers, with Undo.
Mail filing and pause say plainly what they did; Calendar shows several days; Bike + bus is sturdier.
Hub's database is created readable by the owner only.

title: Ask hands cooking and groceries to Kitchen
changes: Ask passes cooking and grocery requests to Kitchen, and Kitchen's cards show in the chat.
A preview Hub for development, on a copy of real data.

title: Three main views: Ask, Today and Insights
changes: Hub's top bar settles on three views: Ask, Today and Insights.
Ask can look up the network, the inbox's size and what the AI has cost.
Insights gains a network summary; Today stops showing a second card for a tool that already asks for a decision.
Trip starts from a made-up sample trip and always keeps the saved one exactly as it was.
An attempt the night before rolled itself back; this release carries the same changes.

title: Ask Hub, a chat that can look things up
changes: Ask Hub: a chat that answers from Hub's own lookups. It can read, not change.
The first release from the cleaned-up history; the source is ready to be public.
